items.text: One drag only: the second handle mirrors the first (S-curve). Then lines build around the curve so it becomes the top of a whole Motion Card; we pull back and its fields fill in (motion, component, easing, duration). Deck and plugin use the full card.

Plugin is now a list of easings by name (as in the case study): the deck pours into it. The cursor picks “moving → slow”, drags it out and it forms a Motion Card between the two screens. Then a pull-back: the plugin slides off, Figma chrome falls away, many flows with specs popping in between screens (cards a bit larger than true scale for the thumbnail).

New order: the deck closes, the Motion Cards plugin panel appears on its own, the cards fly into it and become the list; only then Figma draws itself around the plugin (266–292). Pick, drag and zoom-out follow, 12 frames later.

Composition balance: as the fan collapses, the deck drifts left; the plugin appears right of centre so the two sit as a centred pair; when Figma builds, the plugin glides into its place in the window.
